predecessors.name: Caliphate of Córdoba
predecessors.text: Cliopatria's first Carmona shape (11,162 km2), centred on Carmona and Écija

successors.name: Almohad Caliphate
successors.text: Carmona and its district: the second taifa's capital (the page's 'Capital: Carmona'); Cliopatria's 1147 shape (4,258 km2) lies north-west of Carmona and does not contain it, so a 37 km circle of the…

ledger.x: 1013: the Birzalids found the taifa of Carmona.

c. 1143: Carmona is a taifa again. The page has the second period 'from around 1143 to 1150' after the Almoravid rule of 1091-1143 in the infobox; it names no ruler and no land beyond the capital, so the circle round Carmona is the researcher's reading.
1150: the taifa of Carmona ends; the land passes to the Almohads (see the loss event).

wars.name: Seville's conquest of Carmona
wars.outcome: Seville ended the first taifa of Carmona in 1066 (1067 on the city page).

wars.name: Almohad conquest of Carmona
wars.outcome: The Almohads conquered the second taifa in 1150; Ibn Hamusk held the town briefly before the Almohads regained it in 1161.

certainty.note: The pages name only the capital; no frontier, district or area is given.
